newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden sees economy on track in budget.
newsitem.headline: Sweden sees economy on track in budget.

text.p: The Swedish government unveiled on Friday a 1997 budget that showed the economy recovering at a faster pace, with the country's budget deficit and inflation continuing to fall.

The centre-left government, revealing figures that show it may meet the European Union's criteria for economic and monetary union (EMU), forecast a 1997 budget deficit of 2.6 percent of Gross Domestic Product, a fall compared with a forecast made earlier this year.
Although it announced no new savings when it tabled its 1997 budget on Friday, the Swedish government said the gross state debt would be 78.1 percent of GDP in 1996 and 78.0 percent of GDP in 1997.

The government said inflation would fall to 1.0 percent in 1996, lowering an earlier forecast of 1.9 percent for the year, and said in 1997 inflation would be 2.2 percent compared to an earlier forecast of 2.3 percent.

The horizon would still be clouded by unemployment, however. Sweden lifted its unemployment forecast to 7.7 percent for 1996 and to 6.9 percent in 1997. Previously the government had forecast jobless rates of 7.2 percent and 6.5 percent.
It said public sector finances would be balanced in 1998 and set a target of achieving a surplus in public finances after that.
